comment:
The arch, pylons, anchorage and approach read very well on the site; FORT POINT (plot 0) is the weak part, it reads as a ragged, half-ruined brick shell rather than the massive, intact casemate fort:
1. The outer walls look broken and jagged (notches, stray single blocks, uneven tops). Make them solid, continuous, vertical brick walls with a clean, level top line, one parapet course at the top all the way round.
2. The three tiers of arched gun casemates do not read. On the water-facing north and west fronts, make three clear horizontal rows of regularly spaced openings (every 2 blocks along the wall, one row per tier at y 1, 3 and 5), each a dark recessed opening with a granite sill course under each tier, so the rows read from a distance.
3. Give the landward (south and east) fronts a granite base course and a clean row of narrow loopholes, with the arched sally port clearly framed in granite.
4. The parade ground (the open courtyard) should be visible from above as a clean paved square with arcaded galleries (arches) on its inner faces at each tier.
5. Keep the lighthouse on the top tier at the north-west corner, dark with a lit lantern.
KEEP EXACTLY: the fort's footprint, position and height (its walls to the map, top y 8, lighthouse to y 14, nothing above y 15); and do NOT change anything of plot 1 (the pylons, arch, deck, anchorage, cables, approach).
summary: Rewrote the Fort Point shell (parts/fort-shell.mjs) from the footprint map: solid level brick walls with a continuous parapet and grey coping, three regular rows of dark recessed gun ports on grey sill courses (N/W), grey base course with one row of slits (S/E), a granite-style framed arched sally port, 2-wide arcades on all three tiers of the parade faces. fort-top: lanterns moved inside the parapet, parade border, entrance kept clear. Plot 1 unchanged (all 1,980 changed cells inside the fort box, y<=9).
applied: 1 Walls: every fort cell solid (y1 base, y2..6 bricks); parapet y7 bricks + y8 stone_bricks coping on all outer cells with 8-neighbour edge detection so the stepped corners no longer gap; old embrasure stair bits removed; parapet-top lanterns moved down to the deck (y7) so the y8 top line is clean

2 Casemates: N- and W-facing faces get 1-wide dark openings (air front, black_concrete back) every 2 blocks (odd x / odd z, same columns on all tiers) at y1, y3, y5, with continuous stone sill courses at y2 and y4 (the ground course under tier 1); convex corners and 2-wide risers left as solid piers

3 Landward: stone base course y1 on S/E faces; one row of narrow 1x2 slits (y3..4, recessed 1, black back), centred on each 3-5 long face and every 3 on the long east face; sally port framed with stone_bricks jambs, upside-down stone_brick_stairs arch head and a lintel with chiseled keystones; removed the lamp post that stood in the sally port entrance

4 Parade: stone_bricks paving with a smooth_stone border along the walls; on every parade face run of 4+ cells, 2-wide arches (pier, open, open) stacked on all three tiers with brick_stairs arch heads and black backs (deck top kept brick)
5 Lighthouse kept as it was (dark blackstone, glowstone lantern, rod to y14)
skipped: 'Granite' rendered as grey stone_bricks, not polished_granite: in Minecraft polished_granite is almost the same tone as bricks (the palette check flags it), so granite sills and frames would not read; stone_bricks is in the palette and the brief lists it for trim
Casemate openings are 1x1, not arched: at 0.5 blocks/m there is no room for an arch head on a 1-wide opening; the parade arcades and sally port carry the arches
Parade stays the map's irregular shape (not a true square), and the stepped NW/SE diagonals remain, because the footprint must not change
Stair towers (y9 walls, y10 cap) left as they were; they are the only things above y8 besides the lighthouse
